acceptanceCriteriaCoverage.notes: Implementation provides game loop infrastructure but does not verify AC compliance through tests. Tests check internal mechanics but not AC-specific requirements: 60Hz fixed timestep physics updates, input handling orchestration, collision detection integration, rotating station state management.

findings: ERROR [src/game/game-loop.js:97,101-102,105-107]: Critical defect in update() method: render hooks execute both in the update() error path (line 97, 101-102) and in the render() method (line 105-107), causing render hooks to execute twice per frame. This violates single responsibility - update() should only perform physics/simulation updates, not render operations.

ERROR [src/game/game-loop.js:110-119,115]: Silent error swallowing in executeHooks() method: catch block on line 115 is empty, completely discarding hook errors without logging or recovery. This makes debugging impossible and violates error handling requirements.

ERROR [src/game/game-loop.js:84-103,96-99]: Error handling violation in update() method: when errors occur, the method executes beforeRender hooks (line 97) and immediately returns, bypassing critical afterUpdate and afterRender hooks. This leaves the game loop in an inconsistent state.

ERROR [tests/game-loop.test.js:136-249]: Test inadequacy: tests only verify hook execution order and basic mechanics, but do not verify AC requirements (AC-1 physics-based controls, AC-2 rotating station, AC-3/AC-4 collision detection). Tests check that subsystems exist but do not verify that the game loop properly orchestrates physics, collision, input, and state updates according to the 60Hz fixed timestep requirement.

INFO [src/game/game-loop.js:74-77, tests/game-loop.test.js:293-310]: Fixed timestep implementation correctness concern: while accumulator logic appears correct (lines 74-77), there are no tests verifying that the 60Hz fixed timestep actually produces deterministic physics updates or that multiple updates are correctly handled when frame rate drops.
